successCriteria.description: The JWT middleware verifies a bearer token and, on success, populates request.user with exactly { id: string; role: UserRole } (role one of 'employee' | 'manager' | 'hr_admin'); a missing/invalid/expired token is rejected with a 401 and does not set request.user.

The requireRole(...) guard enforces the full RBAC matrix: employee may act only on their OWN resources; manager inherits all employee permissions and may additionally approve/reject subordinates' requests but never their own; hr_admin may view and act on ALL requests and adjust balances. Each matrix case is covered by a passing Jest unit test in tests/unit/modules/auth/.

Ownership is resolved by comparing the authenticated principal's employee id to the resource's owning employeeId (LeaveRequest.employeeId / LeaveBalance.employeeId); a resource is "own" only when they are equal.
Subordination is resolved via the employee module (B is subordinate of A when B.managerId === A.id); the auth/RBAC code never queries the employees table directly.
Self-approval is explicitly blocked: the approver must never equal the applicant, even when a manager is their own manager.

constraints: RBAC is enforced ONLY at the route level via requireRole(...); no inline role/ownership checks may appear inside services or handlers.
The auth module depends only on shared-types (UserRole enum); it must not import from leave, balance, or any other domain module.
Manager/subordinate lookup goes through the employee module's public entry point (src/modules/employee/index.ts); the auth/RBAC code must not query the employees table directly.
Local dev auth uses seeded local users; no mock OIDC provider is introduced.
No hardcoded secrets: the JWT signing/verification secret must come from configuration/environment, never a literal in source.
Use `unknown` with type guards, not `any`, when decoding the JWT payload into request.user.
outOfScope: No mock OIDC provider; local dev auth is seeded local users only.
No inline RBAC/ownership checks inside services or handlers — enforcement is route-level only.
No leave/balance business logic (create/approve/reject/cancel, balance adjustment) is implemented in this phase — only the auth + RBAC primitives those routes will consume.
No direct employees-table query from the auth module; manager lookup is delegated to the employee module.

entityInvariants.invariant: Always the shape { id: string; role: UserRole } with role restricted to 'employee' | 'manager' | 'hr_admin'; set only by the JWT middleware after successful verification, never by handlers.
Role hierarchy is fixed: manager inherits every employee permission; hr_admin supersedes both. No role may be granted a permission outside this matrix.
B is a subordinate of A iff B.managerId === A.id; this relationship is the sole basis for manager approval authority and is read via the employee module, never recomputed in auth.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Requires a valid bearer JWT; missing/invalid/expired token → 401 and request.user left unset.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Authentication failure → 401 with { error: string; code: string }.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Enforces the role matrix; authorization failure → 403 (code FORBIDDEN).
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Authorization failure → 403 with { error: string; code: string }.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Resource is "own" iff its employeeId equals the authenticated principal's employee id.
Manager may approve/reject only where applicant.managerId === manager.id AND applicant.id !== manager.id (self-approval always denied).

consistencyRequirements.requirement: Reuse the UserRole enum (employee | manager | hr_admin) exactly as defined; do not redeclare or diverge from its values.
request.user must match the auth contract { id: string; role: UserRole }.
Manager/subordinate resolution must use the employee module's manager lookup (findByManager / managerId), not a direct employees-table query.
Error responses use the { error: string; code: string } shape with 401 for auth failure and 403 (FORBIDDEN) for authorization failure.

Self-approval prohibition and manager-only approval follow the binding rule "Only a manager (an Employee referenced by the applicant's managerId) may approve or reject a LeaveRequest; the approver must not be the applicant."

integrationPoints.why: The auth module's role type and matrix are defined against this enum.
Subordination resolution for manager approval authority; the only sanctioned path to the employees table.
The requireRole(...) guard and request.user principal are consumed by leave routes to enforce the RBAC matrix.
